newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Feb 6.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Feb 6.

text.p: The following stories were reported in Thursday's electronic version of The Wall Street Journal:
* Morgan Stanley and Dean Witter confirmed they would merge in a deal valued at $10.22 billion in stock, causing a rally in other brokerage firm stocks.
* A 4.6 percent drop in Intel's shares drove a plunge in technology stocks. The Dow industrials went down 86.58 points to 6,746.90. Bond prices were lower and the dollar was mixed.

* Shareholders are still upset at General Motors' decision not to pay a 20 percent premium in its sale of Hughes Electronics defense business to Raytheon. Implications could be serious because the sale must be approved by 50 percent of Hughes' public owners.
* The Federal Reserve decided against raising short-term interest rates, but some believe the Fed could raise rates soon.
* Ford Motor faces $5 million in daily costs from lost production because of a strike at an automotive seat supplier.
* Toyota Motor is bracing for "severe" shortages of certain models bound for U.S. export because of a brake valve shortage.
* New York's attorney general urged state regulators to block NYNEX's merger with Bell Atlantic.
* Roche Holding agreed to buy the Tastemaker flavor business from Hercules Inc and Mallinckrodt Inc in a deal valued at about $1 billion.
* Mattel Chief Executive Jill Barad plans to shed lagging noncore lines and abandon the emphasis on double-digit quarterly earnings targets.
* CalEnergy, Southern Co and Duke Power are considering bids for all or part of a portfolio of 18 New England power-generating plants owned by New England Electric System.
* Apple Computer is suspending bonuses for top executives and plans much more aggressive advertising.
* Aetna reported a $107.1 million fourth quarter loss, mainly from a charge for its acquisition of U.S. Healthcare.
* Sony's pretax profit nearly doubled in the third quarter.
* Rubbermaid's quarterly profits, hurt by higher resin prices, came in below analysts estimates.
* Confidence about interest rates helped London shares set new closing and intraday highs.
* Medaphis posted a larger-than-expected fourth quarter loss and said it is closing one unit and considering the sale of others.
* Polaroid has hired mergers and acquisitions specialist J. Samuel Ridley.
* Britain's Prudential Corp made a $3.08 billion offer for Scottish Amicable, but Abbey National indicates it will sweeten its $2.27 billion offer in response.
* Some of the rumors about mergers among brokerage firms have been around Wall Street longer than the traders who pass them.

But suddenly yesterday, everyone was taking the chatter a lot more seriously. In the wake of the news that Morgan Stanley Group and Dean Witter are merging, shares of several Wall Street firms were up sharply as investors concluded that the odds went up for more deals. -- Heard on the Street.

* Following the age-old market custom of "buying on the rumor, selling on the news," bonds sold off yesterday after the Federal Open Market Committee announced its widely anticipated decision to leave interest rates unchanged. -- Credit Markets.
-- New York newsdesk 212-859-1610.
